newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Dealers see 6-month Kazakh debt yields unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Dealers see 6-month Kazakh debt yields unchanged.

text.p: A sluggish market and apprehension over pension reform mean yields on Kazakhstan's six-month treasury bills (MKMs) are unlikely to change at auction, dealers in the former Soviet republic said on Monday.
"Operations in the market are very slow so it's unlikely there will be any change," Nurlan Ukhametzhanov, dealer at TuranAlem Bank in the former Soviet republic, told Reuters.
Kazakhstan, an oil-rich country of 17 million, auctioned 600 million tenge worth of six-month T-bills late on Monday but results will be announced only on Tuesday.
The yield on six-month MKMs at the last auction on June 23 rose to 15.05 percent from 14.52 on June 9.
Dealers said they were also waiting to see how the government would pay off 36 billion tenge in debts to pensioners which it has promised to do by the end of this year.
"It depends on how the government borrows," said Sergei Vasilyev, dealer at AO Kazkommertsbank, a large private bank. "If it's non-inflationary, then yields could go up," he said.
